**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Cross-section view of a corn ear (cut end view)
- Kernels arranged in circular pattern around cob pith
- **Prominent pink/reddish-purple discoloration** throughout the cob pith tissue
- White/gray powdery fungal material visible
- Kernels appear pale/cream-tan colored

**Key Diagnostic Feature:**
The pink-to-reddish-purple coloration permeating the cob pith tissue is the hallmark diagnostic feature of **Gibberella ear rot** (*Fusarium graminearum* / *Gibberella zeae*). This pathogen characteristically stains the cob pith pink/red and produces pink-red mold on kernels, distinguishing it from:
- Diplodia (white mold, no pink coloration)
- Aspergillus (olive-green/gray mold)
- Fusarium (scattered white-pink mold but less cob pith staining)

The cross-sectional view showing diffuse pink-red discoloration of the internal cob tissue is a classic and distinctive presentation of Gibberella ear rot.
